question: A shopkeeper bought an article for ₹500. At what price (in ₹) should he sell the article to make 28% profit?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The Cost Price (CP) of an article is always considered as 100%.

Since the shopkeeper makes a profit of 28%, the Selling Price (SP) becomes 100% + 28% = 128% of CP.

⇒ SP = 128% of 500

⇒ SP = 1.28 × 500 = 640

**∴ The correct answer is ₹640.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Cost Price (CP) = ₹500

Profit = 28%

 
 
 

 
 
 
 
 CP = ₹500
 (100%)
 
 
• 
 + 28% Profit
 + ₹140
 
 
 SP = ₹640
 (128%)

**Formula Used:**

Selling Price (SP) = CP × [(100 + Profit %) ÷ 100]

**Calculations:**

⇒ SP = 500 × [(100 + 28) ÷ 100]

⇒ SP = 500 × [128 ÷ 100]

⇒ SP = 500 × 1.28

⇒ SP = 640

**∴ The correct answer is ₹640.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Loss Percentage

Loss happens when the Cost Price is greater than the Selling Price. The formula is: Loss % = [(CP − SP) ÷ CP] × 100.

Marked Price and Discount

Discount is always calculated on the Marked Price (MP) given on the label of an article. The Selling Price is derived as: SP = MP × [1 − (Discount % ÷ 100)].

Successive Discounts

When two successive discounts of a% and b% are applied, the effective single discount is calculated using the formula: [a + b − (a × b ÷ 100)]%.
